title: Water: Finding and Disinfecting
content:
Finding water: Follow terrain downhill - water collects in valleys and low ground. Green vegetation, insect swarms, and animal tracks converging often lead to water. Collect rain and dew. Morning dew can be sponged from grass with a cloth and wrung into a container.

Always assume natural water carries pathogens. Disinfect before drinking.

Boiling is the most reliable method: bring water to a rolling boil for at least 1 minute (3 minutes above roughly 2000 m / 6500 ft elevation). This kills bacteria, viruses, and protozoa.

If you cannot boil:
- Filtering through cloth removes sediment but NOT pathogens.
- Chemical treatment (unscented household bleach, ~2 drops per liter of clear water, wait 30 minutes) is a fallback. Water should have a faint chlorine smell.
- Solar disinfection: clear plastic bottle, full sun, 6+ hours.

Clear water disinfects more reliably than cloudy water, so let sediment settle or pre-filter first. Drink steadily; do not wait until you feel thirsty.
